newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Little changed in listless talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Little changed in listless talk.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was listless on a lack of fundamental changes with most players staying at the sidelines, awaiting market-inspiring news to emerge.
Buying interest was thin though an offer was heard at $103.50 per tonne, traders said.
The 180-cst grade has been capped by the $103.50-per-tonne level last week with few bids and offers and traders attributed the dull market to poor demand.
A local trader who had bought at least five cargoes, seen as routine purchase, has been absence in the market since late last week, traders said.
"There is no other demand, so even supplies are tighter than before, prices fail to move higher," said one trader.
Supplies from the Middle East has started to tighten as fewer cargoes are coming to Singapore with higher Mideast demand for fuel oil for air-conditioning at home in the summer season.
Taiwan's state Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is expected to announce on Tuesday the result for a tender to sell a third 30,000-tonne cargo of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for June lifting.
"The CPC result may give some fresh direction for the market," said one trader.
The swaps market was also quiet.
June swaps were at $100.75/$101.25 against Friday's $100.00/$101.50 and July swaps were at $99.00/$99.50 against $98.50/$99.00.

No transaction was reported on the SIMEX fuel oil futures contract on late Monday. June contract was bid/offered at $100.50/$102.50 and July was at $99.00/$100.00, little changed from their previous levels.
